pages.title: Jupiter moons
pages.text:
The four largest moons of Jupiter
Moon | Diameter (km) | Orbital period (days) | Discovered by | Discovery year
Io | 3,643 | 1.8 | Galileo Galilei | 1610
Europa | 3,122 | 3.6 | Galileo Galilei | 1610
Ganymede | 5,262 | 7.2 | Galileo Galilei | 1610
Callisto | 4,821 | 16.7 | Galileo Galilei | 1610
Notes: NASA credits Galileo Galilei with the discovery of all four in 1610. The orbital periods are rounded to one decimal place in NASA's fact sheet.
Sources
NASA NSSDC, Small Solar System Worlds Fact Sheet (diameters and orbital periods)
NASA Science, Jupiter Moons (discovery and year)
